results.content: 1st Open Call round – Supporting SMEs in the Textile Sector towards Digital and Green Transition

beneficiaryAdministration:
Applications must be submitted exclusively online via the Application Portal https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/FutureProofTextiles-1st-OpenCall

  1. Technical Innovation (40%): Assesses the novelty, feasibility, and scalability of the proposed solution.
  2. Impact & Sustainability (30%): Evaluates the contribution to supply chain resilience, digitalization, and the green transition.
  3. Business Viability (20%): Measures market potential, financial sustainability, and commercialization strategy.
  4. Implementation Feasibility (10%): Reviews SME capacity, resource allocation, and the execution timeline outline.

Coordinated by UNIWA, a five-member international Evaluation Committee ensures a strictly confidential and impartial selection process, free from national or professional conflicts of interest. Applications are evaluated fairly against official criteria, with strict adherence to ESG standards and the EU’s "Do No Significant Harm" (DNSH) principle. Furthermore, selected projects must actively integrate climate-neutral, circular economy practices and strive for gender equality across all personnel levels.
description:
Link to the online Application Portal : https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/FutureProofTextiles-1st-OpenCall

Open Call objective: Empowering 20 SMEs in the textile sector to successfully navigate the "twin transitions" of digital transformation and green sustainability.

Support: Beyond the €60,000 co-financing grant (50 000 EUR – fixed lump Sum Grant, 10 000 EUR – required self-funding by SME), FutureProofTextiles offers extensive capacity-building and networking resources to help build a connected SME ecosystem:

  1. Tailored Training: An average of 40 hours per SME focusing on digital transformation, circular economy principles, and sustainable production.
  2. Dedicated Mentoring: Custom technical consulting and mentoring sessions for up to 6 selected SMEs based on specific needs.
  3. Open-Access Materials: Production of 100 hours of scalable training curricula and best-practice guides for the broader textile sector.
  4. Cross-Border Networking: Facilitation of international collaboration to foster an innovative textile ecosystem.

(Further details regarding these services will be shared with the selected SMEs.)

Who can apply:

Company size

  1. Applicants must fall under the category of SME, according toEuropean Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC*
  2. Partnerships Clusters and intermediary organisations are not eligible even if they are SMEs.
  3. Each applicant should represent a single SME, not a consortia of multiple SMEs.

Industry

  1. Applicants must be SMEs operating in the textile value chain. SMEs from complementary sectors (e.g., tech, machinery) are also eligible, provided their proposed innovation directly contributes to the textile value chain. Activities must align with a relevant NACE code (or national equivalent), such as:
  2. Textile manufacturing: C13.1, C13.2, C13.3, C13.9
  3. Apparel manufacturing: C14.1, C14.3
  4. Textile-based products and technical textiles: C15.12, C22.19
  5. Textile recycling and circularity: C38
  6. Digital and innovative solutions for the textile sector: J62, J63
  7. Manufacture of machinery for textile, apparel and leather production:C 28.94

Location

  1. Only SMEs legally established in countries participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP) are eligible to apply. This includes EU Member States and any other country formally associated with the SMP. A full list of participating countries is published here: List of participating countries in the Single Market Programme (SMP)

Language

  1. The applicant SME must have at least one staff member who speaks English and will be actively involved in the implementation process, handling all communication needs with the consortium.

Submission Rules:

Platform

  1. Proposal submitted online on the EU Survey Platform. Any other means will not be accepted. Application Form

Language

  1. Proposals must be written in English. Submissions done in any other language will not be evaluated.

Submission Limit

  1. Applicant SMEs may submit up to two proposals per Open Call round (one under Green Transition and one under Digital Innovations). Despite this, each SME is eligible to receive a maximum of one grant award across the entire program.

Proposal Requirements

  1. The proposal must demonstrate a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 5 or higher.

Compliance & Ethics

Applicants must confirm their full compliance with all rules, including absence of double funding, and conflict of interest, by reviewing and signing the mandatory forms included in the application:

  1. Funding eligibility and absence of conflict of interest declaration form
  2. SME and Eligibility declaration form

Step by Step Guide

Applicants may submit one proposal for a Green Transition project and one for a Digital Innovation project. Please note that a separate application must be submitted for each.

Step 1: Verify Eligibility

Review the eligibility requirements thoroughly to ensure your organization and project qualify for funding.

Step 2: Concept & Budgeting

  1. Check out “Exhaustive List of Eligible Activities and Eligible Costs” document.
  2. Check out “Needs of the SMEs in the Textile Sector” document, which helps the brainstorming process.
  3. Brainstorm your proposal. When brainstorming, keep in mind that the project implementation period is 9months.
  4. Compose an initial draft, and develop a comprehensive budget based on eligible costs. Clearly define your objectives by establishing specific milestones.

Step 3: Draft Responses

  1. Prepare your answers for each section of the “Standardized Application Form Template” document, before starting the online submission.

Step 4: Prepare Mandatory Documents

Complete and sign the following required forms:

  1. Complete the “Tables with Activities, Budget, Milestones, and Risks” document. Please note that milestones may be subject to negotiation if the proposal is selected, and applicants will not be evaluated based on the proposed milestones
  2. Fill in the “SME and Eligibility Declaration form”.
  3. Fill in the “Funding eligibility and absence of conflict of interest declaration form”.

Step 5: Complete the Online Form

Access the online portal – EU Survey to input your responses. We recommend using a stable internet connection to prevent data loss.

Step 6: Upload Attachments

Attach all mandatory documents from Step 4 into their respective upload fields within the form.

All necessary documents are available for downloading through the Application portal and through the relevant posts in projects LindeIn and ECCP page.

results.content: PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects

beneficiaryAdministration:
Submission: the application form and all supporting documents must be submitted in English, before the deadline, through the EU Survey platform at this link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/PowerUpNetZero_Call_InnovationProjects

An email confirming the receipt of the application will be sent to the main contact person (who filled the application).

In order for the application to be considered eligible, all the following supporting documents must be filled in English, signed and uploaded in the application form before the deadline:

· Activities timeline, budget and KPIs: based on an excel file provided by PowerUp NetZero.

· Declaration of Honour: template provided by PowerUp NetZero, must be signed and dated.

· Result of the SME Financial Viability Self-Check - available at the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/research/participants/lfv/lfvSimulation.do

All documents are availanble at the following link: https://piemonteinnova.it/second-powerup-netzero-open-call-innovation-projects/

The evaluation process consists of:

1.Eligibility check (by 25th September 2026).

2.Evaluation process made by an Evaluation Panel which will evaluate and score the relevance, impact, and implementation sections of the application.

3.Once the evaluation process is completed, all applicants will receive an e-mail about the final results (deadline 19th October 2026).

4.Agreement signature (only for selected applications) with one of the PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects partner of reference (FPI or EnviPark) (deadline 13th November 2026).

Each beneficiary Consortia of this call can receive up to 120.000,00 EUR in the form of a lump-sum (thus, it is expected that at least 14 projects will receive financial support).

Beneficiaries can participate to the different PowerUp NetZero Open Calls (Business Innovation Services and Technology Adoption Activities or Innovation Projects) but a single beneficiary cannot receive more than 60.000,00 EUR overall.

Only one application per SME and Consortia will be accepted under this specific call.

If an entity submits more than one proposal, as a general rule, only the first proposal submitted will be considered eligible for evaluation.

Starting of projects: 16th November 2026, with a duration of maximum 10 months from the signature of the agreement.

The applications selected will be funded until the budget limit of the PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects is reached.

callTitle: PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects
furtherInformation:
The PowerUp NetZero OPEN CALL FOR INNOVATION PROJECTS provides financial support for helping SMEs and start-ups adopt or improve net-zero technologies and solutions (Solar energy, Battery and energy storage, H2 technologies, Sustainable biogas and biomethane, Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)) in their processes, products or services. The call for innovation projects targets companies working together to implement:

  1. PoC or testing of new / improved environmentally friendly products.
  2. Net-zero solutions and services.
  3. Pilot /demonstration actions.

A high degree of innovation is expected in response of this call. Funded activities could address technical risks associated with the demonstration of innovative technologies and solutions, such as optimising technology processes and operational parameters and/or improving the characteristics of their products/solutions. Innovation projects should demonstrate an innovative net-zero technology or solution in an operational or in a Virtual & Industrially Relevant environment (TRL 6-7) but are not necessarily expected yet to reach large scale demonstration or commercial production.

Applicants must be Consortia of minimum two (2) and maximum three (3) SMEs (also including start-ups provided they are SMEs) established in an EU Member State or in a country participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP) at the moment of the call launching date.

Mail to: punz@piemonteinnova.it

results.summary: RENEW-BOOSTER EUROCLUSTER CALL N°2 FOR FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THIRD PARTIES
results.content: RENEW-BOOSTER EUROCLUSTER CALL N°2 FOR FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THIRD PARTIES

beneficiaryAdministration:
More detailed information about the call may be found here

To apply, please complete the submission form on EU SURVEY

Applications may be modified as long as the deadline is respected: you will be able to save and come back later on EU Survey. The platform will be automatically closed at the date and time announced, that is November 30th, 2026, at 5:00 pm CET. Applicants will receive an e-mail confirming that their application has been well uploaded on the platform. Shall you not receive the confirmation e-mail, please contact Benjamin Schmidt at bes@energycluster.dk and copy your local contact point. SMEs applying as a consortium should fill in one proposal. One of the involved SMEs will act as a “coordinator” and will be responsible for the submission of the application.

RENEW BOOSTER Eurocluster innovation mechanism will support projects in the "challenges" call and projects in the "open" call, at least 3 SMEs and up to €60,000 euros per SME.


Evaluation Process and Criteria

All eligible applications will be evaluated by evaluators against the criteria defined in the RENEW-BOOSTER Call Text: Excellence, Impact and Quality and efficiency of implementation. Each criterion is scored from 0 to 10, with a minimum threshold of 6/10 per criterion.

Indicative timeline:

  1. Call deadline: 30 November 2026 (17:00 CET)
  2. Evaluation: December 2026
  3. Results communication: Mid-January 2027
  4. Contract signature: End-January 2027

For full details on the evaluation methodology, scoring, thresholds, and tie-breaking rules, please see the call text


Proposals will be eligible only if all the following conditions are met:

  1. Applicants must be established in one of the following eligible countries: EU-27 + countries participating in the SMP/COSME strand.
  2. Applicants must be SMEs according to the European Union definition of SMEs: the formal definition is available here and the SME self-assessment questionnaire is available here.
  3. Applications must address either the Challenge Call or the Open Call, as described in the Call Text. For applications submitted under the Challenge Call, detailed descriptions of the challenges can be found here or in the EUSurvey submission form.
  4. Applications must be written in English (applications partially written in another language are not eligible) and must not exceed the maximum number of characters stated in each text box of the pre-defined template available on the submission platform;
  5. Applications must be submitted through EU Survey
  6. SMEs may apply individually to the Challenge Call (Strand A). For the Open Call (Strand B), SMEs may apply either individually or as part of a consortium of up to 3 SMEs.
  7. Each SME may submit a maximum of one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Applications submitted under both strands must address different activities and must not result in double funding. Any SME submitting more than one application to the same strand will be automatically disqualified.
  8. No annexes can be submitted other than the ones demanded on the EU Survey platform.
  9. Every applicant organisation needs to be registered on the EU F&T Portal and have a 9-digit Participant Identification Code (PIC). Please find all information PIC number.
  10. This call requires private co-funding. Further information can be found here on page 5-7.
  11. At least 10% of funded SMEs should come from countries or regions other than those represented in the consortium; Denmark, Norway, Poland, France, Bulgaria and Spain.
description:
The two calls will be structured through two distinct funding strands. It is reminded that the cumulative maximum FSTP support per SME under the whole set of RENEW-BOOSTER calls is EUR 60,000. An SME may submit a maximum of one application per strand, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Consequently, an SME may submit one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, provided that the proposed activities are distinct and no double funding occurs.

Strand A (Challenge-driven) follows a two-step process linked to predefined industrial challenges. In Step 1, up to three SMEs per challenge receive €10,000 (with minimum 20% private co-funding) to develop and validate a proof of concept (TRL 6-7). After evaluation and a final pitch, one SME per challenge advances to Step 2 and receives €50,000 (with minimum 40% co-funding) to further develop and scale the solution (TRL 8–9).

Strand B (Open Call) follows a single-stage selection process. SMEs apply bottom-up and can request up to €10,000, €30,000, or €60,000 depending on project maturity, with increasing private co-funding requirements. Projects run up to six months.

Find more here: call text

callTitle: RENEW-BOOSTER EUROCLUSTER CALL N°2 FOR FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THIRD PARTIES
furtherInformation:
The RENEW-BOOSTER project aims at driving innovation and industrialization in three critical sectors that are vital for Europe’s green transition and energy security: Photovoltaics (PV), Offshore Wind Energy, and the associated Energy Networks. At the core of RENEW-BOOSTER is the Accelerator, providing tailored support for SMEs to identify opportunities and develop solutions, strengthening their role in the renewable energy value chain and enhancing resilience.

The project aligns with Europe’s strategic priorities, including reducing critical raw material dependency (Critical Raw Materials Act), advancing climate goals (Green Deal), and supporting re-industrialization (Net Zero Industry Act). RENEW-BOOSTER aims to empower SMEs and accelerate Europe’s twin green and digital transitions.

We reserve the right not to award all available funds or to redistribute them between the different calls, depending on the proposals received and the results of the evaluation.

For answers to frequently asked questions, please visit our FAQ.

title: SOCPL-2026-INFO-REPR
callTitle: Information, consultation & participation of representatives of undertakings
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

The main objective of this call is to develop employees’ involvement in undertakings by raising awareness and contributing to the application of European Union law and policies in this area. The call aims at supporting projects which seek to help accompany through social dialogue at company level the significant changes driven by industry transitions and, in particular, the take-up and effective functioning of European Works Councils. The call shall focus on one or a limited number of topical challenges with a view to maximise both the individual and aggregated impact of the selected projects.

Scope:

Actions to promote European level and strengthened transnational cooperation between social partners that address the following themes would be expected:

- to promote exchange and wider dissemination of knowledge and good practices and to launch actions aimed at supporting the setting up and good functioning of European Works Councils, including the promotion of gender balanced European Works Councils;

- to support workers’ involvement in the anticipation and management of change and the prevention and resolution of disputes in the event of various forms of restructuring in EU level undertakings and groups of undertakings, as required to achieve a just transition, i.e. address challenges brought by the pursuit of EU’s climate objectives (e.g. Council recommendation of 16 June 20225 on ensuring a fair transition towards climate neutrality), and by the digital transformation of economies (e.g. impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on work organisation or working conditions).
